chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into the state of Ihram in months other than the months of Hajj, or from before the Miqat (station) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had designated. He said: 'His Ihram is not invalid. If he wishes, he may return to his family, for I do not see any blame upon him. If he wishes, he may proceed. When he reaches the designated time, let him enter Ihram again and make it an Umrah, for that is better than his returning, because he has already publicly declared his Ihram.'
And it has been narrated that there is a concession (rukhsah) in entering Ihram before the Miqat for one who fears missing the Umrah in the month of Rajab.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.رُخْصَة: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim enters Ihram before the designated Miqat or outside the months of Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the Ihram of one who enters it outside the Hajj months or before the Miqat, offering flexibility to return or proceed. He prefers proceeding and performing Umrah, as the public declaration of intent (Ihram) is not nullified, reflecting the Shia principle of ease (Rukhas) in ritual purity. This ruling underscores the distinction between the state of Ihram and the specific timing of the Hajj season, allowing pilgrims to maintain their spiritual commitment without penalty.
